title: Build your integration
snippet:
1. Follow our Get Started series
By following our [developer Get Started series](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/get_started), you will create a free test account, generate sample data, send a test API request, and more. Here, you’ll also learn about rate limits and error messages, our Postman collection, and other developer tools we offer.

If you want to make your integration accessible to a wider audience and have it featured in the Klaviyo Integration Directory, you need to be a Klaviyo partner. You can apply to become a partner by filling out our [tech partner application form](https://www.klaviyo.com/partners/partner-tech-form) (eligibility varies). Note that if you want to be featured in the integration directory, you must first [set up OAuth](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/set-up-oauth).

- **Is there a platform fee or cost to integrate with Klaviyo?**
There are no platform or API usage fees with Klaviyo, so integrating and testing are free. To learn more about Klaviyo plans, read our guide on [understanding how free and paid plans differ](https://help.klaviyo.com/hc/en-us/articles/360050759151).

title: Klaviyo API: Keys, Scopes, Rate Limits (2026 Guide)
snippet:
The [Klaviyo](https://www.klaviyo.com/pricing) API is a REST interface that exchanges JSON, runs against one Klaviyo account, and lets code, whether a hand-written script or a workflow built in a tool like [Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com), read and change that account's profiles, events, lists and campaigns.
Klaviyo API access is the set of credentials, request limits and versioning rules that govern how code authenticates to a Klaviyo account, how often it may call the API, and which errors it receives when a request is throttled, mis-versioned or not yet processed.

Before any call goes through, it needs an API key, so the first question is whose key it is. **A private key carries scopes chosen at creation**.
A key limited to reading lists can't send a campaign, and whoever created it owns everything it does.
I didn't verify whether Klaviyo charges for calls, so read Klaviyo's pricing page before assuming either way.

Per [Retention Control](https://retentioncontrol.com/blog/klaviyo-pricing/), the free tier covers 250 profiles at $0 per month, so a test account costs nothing. At 500 profiles the plan is $20, and at 1,000 it's $30, so early growth is cheap.
At 5,000 it reaches $100 and at 10,000 it's $150. At 25,000 it's $400, so a duplicate-heavy import at that scale costs real money each month.
## Klaviyo API rate limits by tier
That import also runs into Klaviyo's rate limits. They span from 1 request a second and 15 a minute at XS to 350 a second and 3,500 a minute at XL, according to [Klaviyo Developers](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/rate_limits_and_error_handling), so **each endpoint's tier determines its maximum API throughput**.

### Is the Klaviyo API free to use?
You don't buy API access on its own; it comes with a Klaviyo account rather than as a separately priced product. Your costs follow the account's plan, such as profile counts and send volume.
Check the current pricing page for your plan before you build, because that's where the limits that affect your integration are set.
The practical consequence: a flow that creates many profiles or sends many messages is billed as account activity, whether a person or a script triggered it.

title: Conversations API overview
snippet:
>
>
> The Conversations API is available to approved accounts and apps only. To request access, submit [this form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1Km75VfMTGwDwAItezaCHtxlTfsxfuxGqDWqFLOFRdZQ/viewform). Access is granted either at the **account level** (for customers using a private API key) or at the **OAuth app level** (for approved partners whose app is allow-listed across their install base).

Rate limits
Conversations API endpoints use the **SMALL** rate limit tier: **3 requests/second** burst and **60 requests/minute** steady. See [rate limits](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/rate_limits_and_error_handling) for more information.
##
Limitations
- Only outbound messages can be sent via this API. Inbound messages (received from a profile) are accessible in the conversation history but cannot be created via API.
- Maximum message body length: **1,600 characters** for SMS, **1,024 characters** for WhatsApp.
- The profile must have a valid, consented phone number on the relevant channel. Attempting to send to a profile without consent will return a 400 error.
- The Klaviyo account must have the relevant channel (SMS or WhatsApp) configured and an active sending number.
- Access is gated at the OAuth app level or account level. See Before you begin for details on requesting access.

title: Klaviyo API: Keys, Rate Limits and Error Codes (2026)
snippet:
[Klaviyo](https://www.klaviyo.com/pricing)'s API is a REST API that speaks JSON:API, authenticated with a private API key, which makes it easy to call from scripts or from automation tools like [Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com), and covers:
- profiles
- events
- lists
- campaigns
- flows
- catalogs
Every request must also name a revision in a header, so a call that works today stays on a dated contract rather than whatever the server ships next. Docs: [developers.klaviyo.com](https://developers.klaviyo.com), last checked 2026-11-22.

Give a private key only the objects the job needs. It lives on your server and carries scopes you choose when you create it. A public key (the short site ID) identifies your account for client-side tracking and can't read your data.

If you're building something other Klaviyo accounts install, you need an OAuth app. If the integration is only yours, a private key is the simpler fit. **A leaked private key is a credential leak, so keep it out of front-end code.**
I haven't confirmed a plan-by-plan breakdown, so I'm not going to list one. The practical test is in your account: if you can create a private key under your account's API key settings, you have access.
Everything below works on Activepieces' free plan. [Start without code or a credit card.](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_anchor&ref=%2Fblog%2Fklaviyo-api-keys-rate-limits-and-error-codes-2026)

Per [Succession Media](https://succession.media/guides/klaviyo-pricing/), the monthly price by profile count is:
| Profiles | Price per month |
|---|---|
| 500 | $20 |
| 1,000 | $30 |
| 5,000 | $100 |
| 10,000 | $150 |
| 25,000 | $400 |
| 50,000 | $720 |

Is the Klaviyo API free to use? Klaviyo doesn't bill per API call; the API comes with your account, and your plan is priced on the account itself.
Rate limits still apply, so a bulk job fails on throttling, not on a bill. Checked 2026-11-22.
Can I use the Klaviyo API on a free plan? Yes, a free account can create a private API key and call the API.
Limits tied to the plan still apply, so confirm in your account that the data you need is available before you build on it. Checked 2026-11-22.

title: developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/authenticate_
snippet:
## OAuth
If you're building an app with Klaviyo, use [OAuth](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/set_up_oauth) to provide secure delegated access to users via access tokens (required to enter Klaviyo’s App Marketplace). When setting up OAuth, you must provide designated scopes for each API authorization request you'll want to make.

title: How to create or clone a private API key | Klaviyo Help Center
snippet:
When you create a private API key, choose an access level for each API scope. These access levels determine whether a third party can:
- Have no access to the data or actions covered by that scope.
- View data covered by that scope without making changes (read access).
- View data and create, delete, or make other changes covered by that scope (read/write access).
For example, to subscribe profiles to marketing and add them to a Klaviyo list from another application, use [Bulk Subscribe Profiles](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/reference/bulk_subscribe_profiles). This endpoint requires `lists:write`, `profiles:write`, and `subscriptions:write`. Granting read/write access for these scopes covers this request; you do not need to grant access to unrelated scopes.

what you want to use them for, such as in a password manager.
- Add or edit its scopes.
- If you need different scopes, create a new private API key with the required access. Update any integrations that use the old key and confirm they work before deleting it.
- The creation page starts with **Custom Key** selected. Choose access for at least 1 API scope before creating the key.
If you're not sure which API endpoints, scopes, or permissions you need, please contact a developer or reach out to a[ Klaviyo partner](https://connect.klaviyo.com/) for help.
